subject: language_arts

unit.title: Spelling with suffixes
unit.essentialQuestion: How do I add an ending to a word so it's still spelled correctly?

title: Drop the e (hope → hoping)
objectives: By the end, I can drop a silent e before adding a vowel suffix.

vocabulary.definition: the main word before any ending
vocabulary.example: hope is the root of hoping

vocabulary.definition: a little ending (tail) added to a word
the quiet e on the end that makes the vowel say its long name
vocabulary.example: the e in hope makes the o say 'oh'

vocabulary.definition: an ending that starts with a vowel
cross off the silent e before adding a vowel suffix

emphasize: When a root ends in a silent e, the e must HOP OFF before a vowel suffix moves in.
The model move: cross the e, THEN add the tail.
Pre-empt the misconception 'hopeing'/'bakeing' (kept the silent e). Repeated phrase: 'Drop the e before a vowel suffix.'

keyConcepts: silent-e roots drop the e before a vowel suffix (-ing, -ed, -er, -est)
cross the e first, then add the suffix
reading the wrong form back ('hopeing') shows why the rule exists
misconceptions: keeping the silent e: hope + ing → 'hopeing', bake + ing → 'bakeing'
applying the wrong rule: doubling instead of dropping (hope + ed → 'hopped')
dropping letters from roots that have no silent e
hooks: Write 'hopeing', read it out loud all clunky, then let the silent e HOP off like a kangaroo to fix it.
priorKnowledge: silent e makes the vowel say its long name (Year 1 split digraph)

digital: animated whiteboard with red cross-off of the e

plan.goal: Show the spelling going WRONG ('hopeing'), feel the clunk, then fix it by letting the e hop off; retrieve Lesson 5's just-add rule.
plan.note: Read 'hopeing' deliberately clunkily — the child must hear that it doesn't work before learning the fix.
plan.successCriteria: Child answers 'jumping' for the retrieval and is ready to 'kick the e off'.

script.say: Watch this go wrong, then we'll fix it. Hope plus -ing… if I just stick it on I get h-o-p-e-i-n-g… hopeing. Try reading that — clunky, isn't it? There's no room for both the e and the -ing. So the silent e has to HOP off first. Let's kick it off! But quick memory check from last time — we added tails the easy way. Add -ing to jump.
script.adaptHints: Listen for 'jumping' (no change). If shaky, re-show jump → jumping: 'that root had no silent e, so nothing hopped off. Today's roots DO end in e.' Match the kangaroo-hop energy to the child.

stuckProtocol: If 'jumping' is shaky: re-show jump → jumping from Lesson 5 — 'nothing changed inside the root, we just grew the tail' — then return to hope.

plan.goal: Teach the rule: silent-e root + vowel suffix → cross the e, then add the tail. Model hope → hoping, bake → baking, baked.
plan.note: The red cross-off IS the concrete move — always cross first, add second. Say the repeated phrase every time.
plan.successCriteria: Child can say the rule back: drop the e first, then add the suffix.

script.say: Here's the rule. If the root ends in a silent e, and my suffix starts with a vowel — like -ing, -ed, -er, -est — I drop the e first. Watch hope: cross off the e (it hops away), then add -ing → hoping. Now bake: cross the e, add -ing → baking. And with -ed: bake, cross the e, add -ed → baked. The silent e always hops off to make room.
script.adaptHints: Emphasize the repeated phrase: 'Drop the e before a vowel suffix. Cross it off, then add the tail.' Let the child say 'HOP!' each time the e is crossed.

elements.value: Drop the e before a vowel suffix!

plan.goal: Shared build: the child is the 'e-kicker' — smile + ing, nice + er, ride + ing, saying what happens to the e each time.
plan.note: The child names the move ('cross it off / drop it') BEFORE spelling. Keep the cross-first habit.
plan.successCriteria: Child says 'drop the e' unprompted and spells smiling correctly.

script.say: You be the e-kicker. Take smile and add -ing. First — what do we do to the e? … That's it, cross it off — now add the tail. Let's read it: smiling! Now try nice plus -er… and ride plus -ing.
script.adaptHints: If the child says 'just add it', point at the silent e: 'this root has a quiet e on the end — what does it need to do first?' Never spell it for them.

check.question: Add -ed to hope. What happens to the e first?
check.expectedAnswer: Drop the e, then add -ed → hoped

wrongAnswers.remedy: Read it back — hope-ed, clunky! What has to hop off before a vowel suffix moves in?

wrongAnswers.why: applied the doubling rule instead of drop-the-e
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does hope have a silent e on the end? Yes — so we DROP the e, we don't double. Cross it off first.

plan.goal: The key diagnostic: hope + ed. 'hopeed' means the e survived; 'hopped' means rule mix-up with doubling.
plan.note: After a correct answer, probe WHY the e had to go (to make room for the vowel suffix).
plan.successCriteria: Child spells 'hoped' and can say why the e was dropped.

script.say: Add -ed to hope. Take your time — remember the move.
script.adaptHints: After success, probe: 'Why did the e have to go?' Listen for: to make room for the vowel suffix / the e hops off first.

blocks.explain: The silent e hops off first, then -ed moves in: hoped.

wrongAnswers.remedy: Read it — hope-ed, clunky. Drop the e before a vowel suffix. Cross it off together.
Does hope have a silent e on the end? Yes — so we DROP the e, we don't double. hope → hoped.

wrongAnswers.why: dropped the e AND lost the suffix's e
wrongAnswers.remedy: The e that hops off is the root's e. The suffix -ed keeps its own e: hop… -ed… hoped.

plan.goal: Independent spelling: -ing and -ed on e-ending roots (hope, bake, smile, race), crossing the e first each time and reading each word back.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2. Always have the child read the new word ALOUD — hearing it is the self-check.
plan.successCriteria: Child drops the e correctly in at least three words and reads each back.

script.say: Your turn, e-kicker! I'll send you words that end in a silent e. Cross the e off first, add the tail, then read your new word back to me — every time.
script.adaptHints: Frame the doing-words around the child's interests (baking cakes, riding bikes, racing cars) — never change the spelling words themselves.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'the silent e is still there — it has to hop off.'
Step down: the tutor crosses the e on the board; the child adds the tail.
ONE hint: 'find the silent e on the end and cross it first.'
Re-ask a smaller version (just -ing on bake).
Keep it safe: 'Spotting the silent e is the whole trick — let's find it together.'

plan.goal: Child teaches the rule back; end on an earned win with process praise.
plan.note: Child-led. Tomorrow's contrast (hop → hopping) is seeded but NOT taught today.
plan.successCriteria: Child states: drop the e first, then add the suffix.

script.say: Teach me the rule for words that end in a silent e when we add -ing or -ed. … Exactly! You spotted the silent e every time and kicked it off before adding the tail — that's exactly the rule. Next time, a sneaky one-letter twin trick: hop and hope are about to have a fight!
script.adaptHints: Process praise only — praise the crossing-first habit and reading words back, not 'being clever'.

blocks.prompt: Say the rule out loud like a spelling champion: 'Drop the e before a vowel suffix!'
blocks.target: Drop the e before a vowel suffix

wrongAnswers.remedy: Read it back — bake-ing, clunky! Find the silent e on the end of bake. What does it need to do first?

wrongAnswers.why: doubled the consonant instead of dropping the e
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does bake end in a silent e? Yes — so the move is DROP, not double. Cross the e, then add -ing.

hints: Find the silent e on the end of bake.
Cross the e off FIRST, then add -ing.

reteach.say: Watch the e hop: b-a-k-e… the e hops off — b-a-k — then -ing moves in: baking. Cross first, add second.

block.explain: The silent e hops off, then -ing moves in: smiling.

wrongAnswers.remedy: There's no room for both the e and the -ing. Which one has to hop off?

wrongAnswers.why: doubled the l instead of dropping the e
wrongAnswers.remedy: Smile ends in a silent e — this is a DROP word, not a double word. Cross the e first.

hints: Does smile end in a silent e?
Drop the e, THEN add the tail.

reteach.say: Smile has a quiet e at the end. Before -ing moves in, the e hops away: smil… + ing… smiling. Say it with a big smile!

block.prompt: Here's a word we built: hoping. Read it aloud, nice and smooth.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Reads 'hoping' aloud with a long o (HOH-ping)

wrongAnswers.why: read it as the double-consonant word
wrongAnswers.remedy: Look closely — just ONE p. The e hopped off hope, so the o still says its long name: HOH-ping.

wrongAnswers.why: tried to sound out the dropped e
wrongAnswers.remedy: The e is gone — it hopped away! Only two beats now: ho… ping.

hints: It comes from the root hope.

reteach.say: This word grew from hope — wishing for something. The e hopped off, but the o remembers its long sound: HOH-ping. Say it with me: hoping.

wrongAnswers.remedy: Read it — hope-ed? Two e's squashed together! Cross the root's e off first.
Hope ends in a silent e — so we drop, we don't double. (Hopped comes from hop — no e!)

hints: Hope ends in a silent e — what's the first move?

reteach.say: Smaller step: hope. Cross the e — hop— wait, the letters say h-o-p now, but the word still remembers its long o. Add -ed: hoped. 'I hoped for sunshine.'

wrongAnswers.remedy: Say the rule with me: drop the e before a vowel suffix. Which letter hops off race?

wrongAnswers.why: doubled the c instead of dropping the e
wrongAnswers.remedy: Race ends in silent e — a DROP word. Cross the e, then add -ing.

hints: Race ends in a silent e.

reteach.say: Race — the e is on the end, quiet as a mouse. It hops off, -ing zooms in: racing! Ready, steady, racing.

block.prompt: Match each root to its new word.

wrongAnswers.why: confused with the double-consonant word from hop
wrongAnswers.remedy: Count the p's! Hoping has one p because it comes from hope — the e hopped off. Hopping needs the root hop.
Every root here ends in a silent e. What happens to the e before the tail goes on?

hints: Every root here ends in silent e — every new word dropped it.
Look for the root's first letters inside the new word.

reteach.say: All four roots end in a silent e, so all four new words dropped it. Hope → hoping, bake → baked, smile → smiling, race → racing. Cross, then add — every time.

wrongAnswers.why: kept the silent e — two e's collide
wrongAnswers.remedy: -er starts with a vowel too! Same rule as -ing: what hops off first?
Nice ends in silent e — drop it, don't double. Cross the e, add -er.

hints: -er starts with a vowel — so the same rule applies.
Cross the e off nice, then add -er.

reteach.say: New tail, same trick! -er and -est start with vowels, just like -ing and -ed. Nice: e hops off — nic — add -er: nicer. 'Your writing gets nicer every day!'

wrongAnswers.remedy: Two e's bumping heads! Which one hops off — the root's e or the suffix's e?

wrongAnswers.why: dropped the e but misspelled the suffix
wrongAnswers.remedy: Good — the e hopped off! Now check the tail: the suffix is -est, e-s-t.

hints: -est starts with a vowel, so the silent e must go.

reteach.say: Large, cross the quiet e — larg — then -est marches in: largest. The largest dinosaur, the largest pizza… the rule works every time.

block.prompt: A friend writes: hope + ing = hopeing. What went wrong, and what's the correct spelling?
block.sample: They kept the silent e. Before a vowel suffix like -ing, the e must be dropped: hoping.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: They kept the silent e; drop it first — the correct spelling is hoping

wrongAnswers.answer: Nothing went wrong / it looks fine
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read their word out loud — hope-ing. Hear the clunk? What does the silent e need to do before -ing moves in?

wrongAnswers.why: fixed it with the wrong rule (doubling)
wrongAnswers.remedy: Careful — hopping comes from hop. Our root is hope, with a silent e. What's the drop-e fix?

hints: Read 'hopeing' out loud — what do you notice?
Say the rule: drop the e before a ___ suffix.

reteach.say: Be the spelling detective: the clue is the extra e. Hope ends in a silent e, and -ing starts with a vowel — so the e must hop off before the tail goes on. The fix: hoping, one e gone, job done.

rows: drop the e before a vowel suffix

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level; at level 3, mix -er/-est words with -ing/-ed words.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach with the e crossed off in red on the board, then a level-1 item.
adaptivity.masterySignal: 3+ correct across levels 2–3 including one -ed form and one -er/-est form, each read back aloud → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'drop the e before a vowel suffix'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'the silent e is still there — it has to hop off.'
Step down: the tutor crosses the e; the child only adds the tail.
ONE hint: 'find the silent e on the end and cross it first.'
Re-ask a smaller version (just -ing on bake), then build back up.
Keep it safe: 'Spotting the silent e is the whole trick — let's find it together.'
adaptivity.personalization: Wrap the doing-words in the child's world (baking their favourite cake, racing their favourite car, riding to their favourite park) — the spelling words themselves never change.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable drop-e item; process praise: 'you crossed the e off first every single time — that's the habit of a real speller.'

differentiation.support: The tutor crosses the e; the child adds the suffix. Do -ing on all four roots first, then -ed.
differentiation.stretch: Spell nicer and largest (drop the e before -er/-est) and explain WHY the e goes.

extension: Find two more silent-e words (like, shine) and add -ing correctly (liking, shining).
assessmentEvidence: Child correctly drops the e before a vowel suffix in at least three of four words (e.g. hoping, baked, smiling) and reads each back.
revisitLater: Warm-up for Lesson 7 contrasting hope → hoping (drop e) with hop → hopping (double); feature in the Lesson 9 suffix sort.
